evidence.V1: Bare flared trunk with upswept branches reads as a dead tree in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view shows a clear star of limbs. Recognisable at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Big trunk, medium 5 branches, small twigs, grain stripes and an end-grain cap on the snapped top: clear hierarchy.
evidence.V3: Stylised, but the limbs are smooth uniform horn/tusk shapes with pointed tan tips, and one lower limb hooks back toward the trunk like a claw; reads more antler than wood, only partly convincing.
evidence.V4: Trunk bark grooves are soft, but branch tips are needle-sharp points and branch-to-trunk junctions are hard, unblended intersections; inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Fork close-up shows branches as separate tubes jammed into the trunk with hard seams and a visible blunt branch end (dark hooked stub on the left limb); roots close-up shows a jagged folded notch on the left side of the root flare.
evidence.V6: Bark brown in 2-3 values (body, groove, light tips/end-grain); disciplined, and the ash/birch colourways stay within one hue.
evidence.V7: 1368 tris vs tree target 2000 (ceiling 5000): under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material and kit palette, but branches are not fused smooth shells as the nature kit specifies, and the needle tips clash with the soft kit look; minor mismatch.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre: correct.

artifacts: Hard unblended seams where branches enter the trunk
Visible blunt branch stub on the left lower limb at the fork
Jagged folded notch on the left side of the root flare
top_fixes: Fuse branches into the trunk (union/remesh or a flared collar at each junction) so joins are smooth shells
Round off the needle tips into blunt broken-off stubs and add slight kinks so limbs read as wood, not horns
Clean the root-flare notch and give the flare 3-4 distinct root buttresses
